# 4 Maccabees Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Mother's Speech Recalled

---

**16:1** If then a woman, old and widowed in mind, having borne seven children, endured beholding them tortured to death, it must be agreed that devout reason is sovereign master of the passions.

**16:2** Thus I have demonstrated that not only men have exercised reason over the passions,

**16:3** but that even a woman despised the greatest pains. And the lions around Daniel were not so savage, nor was the burning fiery furnace of Mishael so intensely hot,

**16:4** as the burning desire of the mother for her children; for she watched seven sons die.

**16:5** But with the reasoning of religion the mother quenched passions so great and many.

**16:6** Consider this also: if this woman, though a mother, had been faint of soul, she would have lamented over them and perhaps spoken thus:

**16:7** Ah, wretched me, and thrice wretched, who having borne seven children, am now the mother of none.

**16:8** O seven pregnancies all for nothing! O seven months of labor and weariness, all in vain!

**16:9** Fruitless have been my nursings and wretched my sucklings; in vain, my sons, I endured for you many pangs of birth,

**16:10** and more grievous ones in your upbringing, and these more grievous still in all your painful deaths.

**16:11** None of my sons will close my eyes; none will lay me in the tomb.

**16:12** But this blessed and holy woman, holding her reason firm, spoke no such words.

**16:13** She did not weep or moan or say anything unworthy; she did not yield to grief.

**16:14** Instead she urged each of her sons on to his death for the sake of piety.

**16:15** O mother, faithful soldier of God! O elder woman, mighty in battle! O woman stronger than all the men!

**16:16** You endured seeing your children die for piety; you gave up your whole family for God's sake!

**16:17** Was it not you, mother of those sons, who encouraged each one of them on his way to martyrdom and called out to each by name?

**16:18** You said to them: My son, do not flee from me, for I wish to see your noble death. And through me you offered them as a kind of burnt offering to God.

**16:19** O mother who alone surpassed all women in courage! O mother of seven children, most noble and most blessed!

**16:20** For what mother has ever seen seven sons die in a single day and has been so possessed by the spirit of devotion to God that she could call them to die thus?

**16:21** You proved that reason is the sovereign master of the passions, O mother, through your holy sons.

**16:22** For these children of yours, like the wind and the tide, have driven out the ungodly Antiochus with their reason and piety.

**16:23** For there are none like these among men or women in all of human memory; none who overcame the passions so completely.
